previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, multiple abdominal surgeries, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and PTSD was admitted with high fevers, confusion, cough, and shortness of breath. Chest imaging revealed multifocal pneumonia in the right lung. Despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, she continued to spike fevers, prompting consultation with infectious disease and pulmonology. A bronchoscopy was performed, during which pus was observed, and BAL cultures confirmed MRSA. She was transitioned to oral linezolid and levofloxacin, with improvement in fever and oxygenation. Her chronic abdominal pain, related to adhesions, was managed with Dilaudid, and medications with serotonin syndrome risk were discontinued. She was discharged home on antibiotics, home oxygen, and follow-up appointments, with stable mental status and ambulatory independence.
problems: Methicillin resistant pneumonia due to Staphylococcus aureus

There is no evidence of focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced
scan.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is not visualized.
